## 629ec8fd452e

**Reproduced shortcut — “bbox gap and at least 8 cells” fits the canonical and generated lessons.** Consider the rival: keep a component exactly when its strict bounding-box interior has a missing cell and the component has at least eight cells. It matched all 4 canonical train/test pairs and matched the intended Python rule on 600 sampled generated scenes (200 per easy/medium/hard).

The reason is a fixed size separation in the current generator: true-hole components have 8, 9, or 14 cells, while the sole open almost-ring distractor always has 7. Solid distractors have no missing bounding-box interior. Thus the thresholded bbox heuristic survives all four declared witnesses even though it is not the topological rule.

I checked an exact 9×12 counterexample containing a closed 3×3 color-2 frame (8 cells, true hole) and an open 3×4 color-3 frame missing one border cell (9 cells, no true hole). The canonical Racket authority keeps only the color-2 frame; the rival also keeps the open color-3 component. The exact grid passes both `self_check` and `strict_canonical_like`, so it belongs to the documented generator domain. `checks/audit/629ec8fd452e/analysis.json` records the canonical-fit and 600-draw census; the input, supported `arcpuzzles apply` output, and rival output are beside it as `input.json`, `racket.json`, and `rival.json`.

A future repair should vary open leaking shapes across the true-hole size range—for example, include an open 3×4 frame with 9 cells—or declare and refute this combined size/topology rival. I made no change to the audited target.

## 629ec8fd452e

**Reproduced curriculum/domain gap — no patch applied because this is an audit target.**
A plausible undeclared shortcut is:

> Keep a component when its strict bounding-box interior has any missing cell
> and the component has at least eight occupied cells.

This shortcut fits all **4/4 canonical labeled pairs** and all **720/720**
ordinary generated inputs checked across easy/medium/hard, seeds 0..29, and
sample indices 0..7 at generator SHA-256
`0007b7a95ed5b13453d55374e1bf72d53a439a03f7844d19c3cf34e3b227feab`.
The reason is structural: the sampler's only open negative is always the same
3x3 almost-ring with seven cells, while every hole-bearing template has at least
eight cells.

The exact 10x14 counterexample in
`checks/audit/629ec8fd452e/comparison.json` passes both `self_check` and
`strict_canonical_like`. It contains a valid closed 3x3 frame, a solid 3x3
negative, and an open 4x4 almost-ring with eleven cells. The selected Racket
authority erases the open ring, while the shortcut keeps all eleven of its cells.
The supported `arcpuzzles apply` receipt is
`checks/audit/629ec8fd452e/racket.json`; executed/catalog rule hash
`83b51fc36bb6` matches.

The exact counterexample is inside the documented validator/teaching envelope
but is **not emitted** by the current sampler. This is a teaching-distribution
finding, not a wrong-label finding. A future repair should vary open-ring size
and gap geometry and declare/test the combined size-plus-bbox rival.

Teaching-support gap, not wrong sampled labels. Targets unchanged.
